results.name: gif-pipeline
notes: Independent pattern process animates at 30fps. Acquisition only waits for its own timer, BitBlts actual desktop RGB, timestamps completion, and transfers ownership through eight preallocated raw frame slots to one encoding worker. No per-frame DwmFlush, pattern generation or pixel validation runs on the acquisition thread.

Worker decodes the source frame ID from captured pixels and verifies every RGB pixel against that known pattern BEFORE writing. Unknown/torn/occluded frames are rejected without persisting their pixels. WIC validation runs offline after recording; no synthetic frames replace captures.

Source QPC intervals describe GDI submission, not DWM presentation. source_snapshot_bracket_changed counts differences between the snapshots read before and after capture. Changed/unavailable brackets, duplicate IDs and IDs outside brackets report correlation ambiguity only: they cannot establish which source update was presented during capture, measure compositor latency, or identify an occlusion cause.

GIF delays use actual capture-completion timestamps with carried 10ms remainder, from first verified completion through recording stop. Zero-delay samples are coalesced; rejected or queue-skipped intervals extend the previous verified frame. Leading acquisition latency is excluded from the captured timeline.

This bounded one-worker prototype measures capture/encode separation. P5 still requires differential frames, worker-pool scheduling, cursor and recording UI. Performance acceptance additionally requires a local physical-display environment, enforced centrally by the report runner.
